images.title: Ways to travel
images.purpose: Show the eight vehicles of the chapter's travel picture, each with its name, so the student sees how many different ways there are to travel.
images.composition: Eight vehicles in a neat grid of 2 rows and 4 columns on white, each with its name written under it.
images.exact_structure: Plain white 16:9 canvas with a grid of exactly 8 pictures in 2 rows of 4, evenly spaced, each with its name centred under it. Flat illustration style, thin dark outlines, colours from the chapter palette plus white and grey. TOP ROW, left to right: (1) a ship with a sail: a red and white hull on a strip of blue water, one mast, one cream triangular sail, a small red flag; (2) an aeroplane: a white passenger aeroplane with a blue stripe, side view, flying to the right; (3) an electric bike: a bike with two black wheels and a green battery box; (4) a train: a blue engine seen from the front and side with yellow and black stripes on its nose, on a short piece of track. BOTTOM ROW, left to right: (5) a bus: a white bus with a blue stripe and a row of windows, side view; (6) a submarine: a dark teal submarine with one tower, half under blue waves; (7) a space shuttle: a white shuttle with an orange tank and two boosters, standing upright with a small puff of smoke below; (8) a sled pulled by dogs: a wooden sled with one person in a red hat standing on it, pulled by exactly 4 dogs in a row, on a white snowy ground. No other objects, no people other than the sled driver.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: There are many ways to travel, and each vehicle suits the place it goes.
images.description: Eight vehicles: a ship with a sail, an aeroplane, an electric bike, a train, a bus, a submarine, a space shuttle and a sled pulled by dogs.
images.context: Starting point is the chapter's own picture of vehicles, in the same eight. The names under each are added so that the picture reads without the text. The book's spacecraft is drawn as a space shuttle, as in its picture.
images.teaching_notes: Ask: which of these would you use on water, in the air, in snow, under water, in space? Link each to a place, as in the worked example: boats for crossing water, submarines deep under water, spacecraft for outer space.

image_decisions.why: The chapter's own picture of eight vehicles is the visual that makes the means of travel concrete.
